title: Fallback decision matrix and customer action snippets (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This draft is a compact, action-oriented decision matrix plus short customer-facing snippets to accelerate status page updates and post-incident customer messages when model fallbacks, regional routing or cache inconsistencies occur. The goal is to reduce triage-to-communication time and give CS teams pre-approved language and a clear escalation decision tree.

Scope and assumptions:
- Intended for incidents that affect tenant inference quality or latency (model fallbacks, region failovers, cache staleness).
- Not a replacement for technical postmortems — this is the customer-facing short form for status pages and enterprise touchpoints.
- Assumes engineering has validated preliminary root cause and risk of rollback/rollforward options.

Quick decision matrix (one-page):
1) Symptom buckets (what customers see):
   - A: Silent degradation — increased hallucinations or wrong-format outputs, no errors returned.
   - B: Elevated latency/p95 spikes or streaming stalls.
   - C: Partial failures — some requests receive 5xx or model-mismatch fallbacks.
   - D: Complete region outage or auth failures.

2) Initial severity assessment (CS + Eng quick check, <15 minutes):
   - A (low-medium): check eval-set mismatch alerts + sample tenant traces. If >1% erroneous outputs for a high-impact tenant, treat as medium.
   - B (medium): confirm p95>target and check if backlog queued.
   - C (high): confirm 5xx rate >0.5% or model fallback count >threshold.
   - D (sev-high/critical): region unreachable or auth errors across tenants.

3) Routing decision and communication cadence:
   - A -> Notify via statuspage "Degraded responses" (informational), send targeted email to affected enterprise customers if sustained >2 hours, include safe-mode suggestions (below).
   - B -> Statuspage incident (investigating), open dedicated customer channel for top-10 affected tenants, provide mitigation checklist and ETA every 30-60 minutes.
   - C -> Statuspage incident (service degraded), CS war room for critical tenants, propose immediate model rollback or routing to verified variant if available; provide replay toolkit.
   - D -> Major incident, page on-call SRE and CS leads, publish a clear service-unavailable notice with recommended failover.

Customer action snippets (short, paste-ready). These are intentionally concise so engineers/CS can use them in status updates, emails, and in-product banners.

Status page: minor/degraded (A)
- "We are seeing degraded response quality for a subset of requests. Our engineering team is investigating and collecting examples. If you notice incorrect or malformed outputs, please use the customer-replay link (below) to submit a sample request. We will provide updates every 2 hours.
- Impact: occasional incorrect responses for a small subset of requests. No authentication or request failures reported.

Status page: investigating (B)
- "We are investigating elevated latency affecting inference in region EU-WEST-1; some streaming responses may be delayed. Engineers are collecting traces and scaling routing to reduce latency. We will post updates every 30 minutes. If your application is latency-sensitive, see suggested mitigations below.

Status page: service degraded (C)
- "We’re experiencing degraded service where some requests fail or are routed to a fallback model variant that may return lower-quality responses. We are prioritizing critical tenants and recommending temporary configuration changes (see email snippet). We will follow up with a detailed timeline and post-incident summary.

Status page: outage/major (D)
- "We are experiencing a regional service disruption. Our team is actively working on restoring full service. For enterprise customers, a support representative will reach out with specific guidance and mitigation options.

Email snippet to enterprise customers (short + actionable)
Subject: Brief service notice — temporary impact to inference quality
Hi <CustomerName>,
We want to let you know we’re investigating an issue affecting inference quality for some requests in <region>. Engineers have identified routing to a fallback model variant for a subset of traffic which may produce lower-quality outputs.
Actions you can take now:
1) Pin requests to a verified model variant: change model parameter to <model-id-stable> in the short term (instructions below).
2) If you have replay/exemplar prompts, upload them via this link so we can prioritize evaluation: <replay-link>.
3) If you prefer we pause traffic to your tenant while we remediate, reply to this thread and we’ll coordinate.
We’ll follow up with a full incident summary within 48 hours.
Best,
Aisha (Redwood Customer Success)

In-product banner copy (for short windows)
- Heads-up: We’re seeing intermittent response quality issues. We recommend pinning to a stable model for the next few hours.
- If immediate rollback is performed, banner: We reverted to a stable model variant — some requests may be slower while caches warm.

Mitigation checklist (engineers + CS quick actions)
- Collect sample failing requests (tenant id, request id, model version, timestamp). Use evidence format: tenant, request-id, prompt-hash, model-id, response snippet.
- Evaluate quick rollback feasibility: is model variant in catalog with compatibility? estimate time to route = 10-30 minutes.
- Temporary config options to suggest customers: pin model, reduce max_tokens, disable streaming (if streaming causes truncation issues), increase timeout.
- Apply short throttles or circuit-breaker to high-volume tenants only if retries create cascading failure.

Replay/evidence upload instructions for customers (short form)
1) Go to <replay-link> and include: tenant id, request id(s), sample prompt(s), timestamp, observed output.
2) Mark severity: low/medium/high. High -> we prioritize and reach out within 1 hour.

Post-incident customer summary template (to send after RCA is complete)
Subject: Incident summary: <date> — impact & remediation
Hi <CustomerName>,
Summary: On <date/time> Redwood experienced <brief cause phrase>. Impact: <how many requests/tenants affected, symptom>.
Root cause: <high-level cause — e.g., model artifact mismatch during canary rollout, cache eviction race in prefix cache>.
What we did: immediate rollback to <model-id>, increased routing isolation, fixed cache eviction threshold and added a TTL sanity check.
Customer impact: We identified X tenants with >Y% incorrect responses and directly notified them. No customer data was exposed.
Next steps: configuration change for pinned models, monthly regression checks added to the model-onboarding pipeline, extended monitoring for output-format drift.
If you’d like a dedicated technical debrief with your engineering team, reply and we’ll schedule.

Escalation and ownership:
- CS lead: Aisha Patel (pager: CS-PG1)
- SRE on-call: (link to rotation)
- Exec escalation: notify Director of Product + Head of Customer Success if incident lasts >4 hours or >5% tenants affected.

Communication guidance (do/don't)
Do:
- Use plain language and be explicit about user-visible symptoms.
- Give customers immediate, practical mitigations.
- Provide a clear timeline for updates and a final postmortem window (48–72 hours).
Don't:
- Avoid technical jargon in the initial status update (save detailed logs for follow-up).
- Don't promise exact ETA until SRE confirms a remediation path.

Appendix: sample decision checklist for CS on call (ticklist)
- [ ] Confirm incident tag and initial severity (A/B/C/D)
- [ ] Gather 3 example requests from each affected tenant
- [ ] Share initial statuspage message (choose the right snippet above)
- [ ] Offer pin-to-stable option to affected enterprise customers
- [ ] Log all customer escalations to CS incident ticket (JIRA: CS-4821)
- [ ] Schedule post-incident debrief within 72 hours

Notes / open questions (for eng follow-up)
- Should we automate the "pin-to-stable" recommendation in the console when a fallback is detected? (product/eng discussion)
- Is there a safe default TTL for prefix cache to avoid mass invalidation?

This doc is intentionally compact so CS reps can copy/paste. For larger incidents we should link to the full technical timeline and artifacts in Confluence.

End of draft.
